908091baae: The State Department expresses its “concern” after four communist ministers join the Mauroy government. Paris denounces interference.
908892ebdc: Commerce bans the export of HBM memory to China and adds 140 Chinese entities to the Entity List.
90ddf5ded1: Consulting services and Russian media targeted
Washington bans the provision of accounting, consulting and management services to Russia and sanctions the channels Channel One, Rossiya-1 and NTV.
90f0b5fec7: Strikes and riots start in Daegu and spread across the South. The American military government proclaims martial law and has the movement suppressed by the police and its troops.
9109bd8257: The Navy acknowledges that an aircraft fired depleted uranium shells on the Vieques firing range, in violation of its own rules.
912dd82686: Switzerland receives one of the highest rates imposed on a Western country, after a tense exchange between Trump and the president of the Confederation.
913a5ab050: During Zelensky's visit to Washington, the United States announces $1.85 billion in aid including a first Patriot battery.
9146603158: The day after Maduro's disputed reelection, an executive order bans the purchase of debt owed by the Venezuelan government and PDVSA.
916a368ecb: The French counterpart of Demagnetize, this Psychological Strategy Board plan aims to weaken the Communist Party and the CGT by clandestine means.
9179336018: Elliott Abrams appointed special envoy for Venezuela
Mike Pompeo appoints Elliott Abrams, convicted in the Iran-Contra affair, to lead regime-change policy in Venezuela.
918e5bc573: Lieutenant Colonel Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba had taken part in several US training courses and exercises, AFRICOM confirms. He overthrows President Roch Marc Christian Kaboré.
91a97c9e4e: A $400 million USAI package funding the refurbishment of 45 T-72 tanks in the Czech Republic and Hawk anti-aircraft missiles.
91c6ca41e8: During the invasion, the Cambodian town of Snuol is destroyed by American aircraft and armor.
91d73b4a01: The CIA pays for more than half of Eduardo Frei's campaign and funds a “scare campaign” against Allende. The Church Committee established this.
91f3af7807: The Treasury announces its largest round of sanctions against North Korea: 56 targets, mostly ships and shipping companies.
9208d22ffe: In an open letter, Ambassador Charles Kushner reproaches Emmanuel Macron for inaction against antisemitism. Paris summons him for interference in its domestic affairs; he sends another diplomat.
922e8784ca: Truck driver killed at Manas base
A U.S. airman, Zachary Hatfield, shoots Kyrgyz driver Alexander Ivanov dead at a checkpoint. He claims self-defense and escapes Kyrgyz justice.
92316f4e1d: Kaspersky targeted by the NSA and GCHQ
The two agencies reverse-engineer antivirus software, including Kaspersky's, and monitor its emails to get around its protections. Revealed by The Intercept in June 2015.
924d3cd870: Putin presents the revelations about his circle as a provocation by U.S. institutions; WikiLeaks points out that the OCCRP, a partner in the investigation, receives funds from USAID. The State Department denies any involvement in the leak.
9252f597e1: The war logs published by WikiLeaks reveal this secret unit tasked with killing or capturing targets from a list, and several raids that killed civilians. The Pentagon condemns the leak without disputing the documents.
9253d297d0: After the ceasefire in Vietnam, B-52s bomb Cambodia massively. Congress imposes a halt as of 15 August 1973.
926e7e4490: An American special forces mission recommends creating paramilitary groups to carry out “sabotage and terrorism” against Communist supporters. The report is declassified.
92880f70b5: Visas denied over Cuban medical missions
Marco Rubio extends visa restrictions to Cuban and foreign officials linked to Cuban medical missions, which Washington calls forced labor.
92b39dadb6: Declassified documents published by the National Security Archive show that the CIA admits the 1953 coup was carried out “under CIA direction.”
92e728d4c7: This NSA program, launched in May 2011, taps a cable between Western Europe and the Far East: 57.7 billion records in one month. Its exact location is not public. Revealed by the book “Der NSA-Komplex” by Spiegel journalists in 2014.
92f747bf34: Executive Order 13692 declares that Venezuela constitutes an “unusual and extraordinary threat” to U.S. security and sanctions seven officials. It serves as the basis for later sanctions.
9305c2d8d2: CIA flights via Palma de Mallorca

According to the Diario de Mallorca, more than 100 CIA flights stop over at Palma, including the one that transfers Khaled el-Masri to a secret Afghan prison. Judge Ismael Moreno provisionally closes the investigation for lack of identification of the crew.
931c0ea7b4: Threat to cut credit to Italy
At the Puerto Rico summit, Washington, London, Paris and Bonn agree to refuse any loan to Italy if the PCI enters the government. Helmut Schmidt reveals this agreement.
9320561791: The CIA's Desmond FitzGerald has an exotic seashell stuffed with explosives studied, to be placed where Castro dives. The project is judged unfeasible. The Church Committee describes it.
9321b64743: North Korean cargo ship Wise Honest seized
The Justice Department announces the seizure of the bulk carrier Wise Honest, accused of exporting coal in violation of sanctions. It is the first seizure of a North Korean ship by the United States.
93340e3849: A Senate committee investigates the occupation of Haiti and Santo Domingo. It gathers testimony of torture and executions, but recommends continuing the occupation.
93356454c1: With the help of the embassy in Caracas, the NSA gains access to the internal communications of the Venezuelan state oil company and targets its executives. Revealed by The Intercept and teleSUR in November 2015.
93461bdb60: Two weeks after the first, a new draft demanding an immediate halt to construction at Har Homa is blocked by the United States.
9347f65c1c: Sabotage in Hanoi Before the French Departure
Before Hanoi is handed to the Việt Minh, Lansdale's agents contaminate the bus company's fuel and prepare arms caches, according to their own report.
9362ebb22d: Human Rights Watch documents night raids by Afghan forces trained by the CIA, who summarily execute civilians and call in strikes on religious schools.
9381761db8: Veto on humanitarian pauses in Gaza
The United States blocks a Brazilian draft calling for humanitarian pauses in Gaza, on the grounds that it does not mention Israel's right to defend itself.
93880b8574: In the midst of the “maximum pressure” campaign, Washington sends a carrier strike group and bombers to the region to deter Iran, opening a crisis in the Persian Gulf.
93b118fda3: According to General Dan Caine, Cyber Command and Space Command were the “first movers,” disrupting Iranian communication and sensor networks before the strikes.
93b5c0cbf6: US forces board the tanker Tifani, loaded with 2 million barrels of Iranian oil at Kharg, between Sri Lanka and Indonesia, more than 3,000 km from the Gulf.
93da77f59b: The largest air raid of the war hits Pyongyang with more than 1,400 sorties in a single day, as part of the “air pressure” strategy.
94084dd3eb: Abrogation of the Bates Treaty with Sulu
Washington unilaterally abrogates the 1899 treaty that guaranteed the autonomy of the Sultanate of Sulu, and places the Moros under direct military administration.
940a604cee: After months of pressure from Trump, Ukraine signs an agreement that creates a joint investment fund fed by its natural resources.
9413f72e41: Aid to Milei conditional on the vote
Trump says he will not be “generous” with Argentina if Javier Milei loses the midterms, while Washington opens a $20 billion swap line for him.
941a227a65: After the nationalization of the International Petroleum Company, an Exxon subsidiary, Washington quietly blocks international credit to Peru until the 1974 Greene agreement.
9432d63889: Secret funding of the Chilean opposition
Between 1970 and 1973, the CIA pays about 8 million dollars to the parties, business associations and media opposed to Allende, according to the Church Committee.
944e35079f: Mike Pompeo proposes a transitional government without Maduro or Guaidó, in exchange for a gradual lifting of sanctions. Caracas rejects the plan.
94879fe2d5: After the Oval Office clash with Zelensky, Trump suspends military aid and then intelligence sharing to force Kyiv to negotiate. Both resume a week later.
95015dbaa3: George Bush orders the Coast Guard to return to Haiti refugees intercepted at sea, without examining their asylum claims. The Supreme Court upholds the practice in 1993.
9505c6f802: A presidential memorandum orders preparation of retaliation against digital taxes and European digital rules that target US companies.
9511d28bf4: Italy is one of the first customers of Crypto AG, a Swiss company secretly owned by the CIA and the BND. According to the Washington Post and ZDF in 2020, its encrypted communications were read, despite its status as a NATO ally.
955100e93f: Three detainees are found dead; the military concludes they were suicides, which a commander calls an “act of asymmetric warfare.” Guards have disputed this account.
955419ba44: Captain Vladimiro Montesinos passes military information to the United States. He is dismissed from the army and imprisoned.
9561d404cb: After paying $340 million to the New York regulator in August, the British bank pays $327 million to federal authorities for Iranian transactions.
9568972eb2: Guaidó calls on the army to rise up. Mike Pompeo and John Bolton publicly back him and claim that Maduro was ready to flee; the operation fails.
958af2b6cb: Wilson refuses to recognize the regime that emerged from Federico Tinoco's coup. Isolated, it falls in 1919.
95901bccd6: According to Iranian authorities, US strikes destroy the pumping station and transformer of the Bunji desalination plant: 20 villages, about 10,000 people, left without water.
9592a45b74: A 1985 CIA assessment attributes the attack on John Paul II to the USSR via Bulgaria. In 1991, analysts testify to the Senate that it was slanted under Robert Gates.
959664b6ed: A report commissioned by Kennedy recommends Americanizing Micronesia, a UN trust territory, to ensure a vote in favor of permanent association. It leaks in 1971.
95f15c62d9: B-29s simulate atomic bomb drops on North Korea with dummy or conventional bombs, to test a battlefield nuclear strike.
961031336a: A landing force protects American lives and property as Turkish nationalists enter Smyrna. Listed in Congressional Research Service report R42738.
962511577d: The largest USAI package to that date: $2.98 billion, including six additional NASAMS systems and drones, to be delivered over several years.
9634bac35f: Collision of USS Baton Rouge off Murmansk
The American submarine Baton Rouge, on a listening mission, collides with the Russian submarine Kostroma near Russian territorial waters. Washington acknowledges the incident.
96365f5fac: Abduction of Abu Omar in Milan
CIA agents abduct the imam Abu Omar and send him to Egypt, where he is tortured. Italian courts convict 23 Americans in absentia in 2009.
9656d86ee0: Operation Valuable/BGFiend: the CIA and MI6 infiltrate Albanian exiles until 1953. Betrayed notably by Kim Philby, most are captured or killed.
965f7a2ad2: Operation Focus: leaflet balloons over Hungary

The CIA-funded Free Europe Committee launches balloons from Bavaria carrying more than 16 million leaflets signed by a fictitious opposition movement, the NEM, calling for passive resistance. Budapest protests to Washington.
9669c9ca8b: After militias storm the US embassy in Baghdad, paratroopers of the 82nd Airborne Division are sent to the region. Listed in Congressional Research Service report R42738.
967f514c50: Execution of detainees, Operation Iron Triangle
Soldiers of the 101st Airborne Division execute three handcuffed Iraqi prisoners. Four are convicted.
968fc9209f: Between April 1922 and November 1923, Marines land five times to protect Americans during unrest. Listed in Congressional Research Service report R42738.
96a4d8ce07: Siad Barre's army, partly equipped by the United States, bombs Hargeisa and massacres thousands of Isaaq. Congress subsequently freezes military aid.
96d1378d88: P4M Spy Plane Shot Down at the Shengsi Islands
Chinese fighters shoot down a U.S. Navy P4M Mercator on a nighttime electronic intelligence mission off Zhejiang. All 16 crew members die.
96fbef0922: Musk hosts Alice Weidel on X
Ahead of the German federal election, Elon Musk, chosen to lead DOGE, talks live on X with AfD candidate Alice Weidel and urges people to vote for her party.
972d15cc54: CENTCOM announces that an Iranian Jamaran-class corvette is “sitting at the bottom of the Gulf of Oman” at its Chabahar pier. Trump makes the “annihilation” of the Iranian navy a war goal.
972fdc17c3: Thousands of political prisoners are shot by the South Korean police at Golryeong-gol. An American officer photographs the executions; the photos are declassified in 1999.
973fa0c691: USS Grayling collision in the Barents Sea
The USS Grayling, tracking a Russian ballistic missile submarine, rams it. Yeltsin protests and Clinton expresses regret.
9741d2e68f: Missiles on Serb radars at Knin
On the first day of the Croatian offensive, US Navy EA-6Bs and F/A-18s fire anti-radar missiles at Serb air defence sites at Knin and Udbina, after being locked on by their radars.
97537e3b0a: Retired colonel James Steele, a Salvador veteran, oversees Iraqi commandos accused of torture and of death squads. Investigation by the Guardian and the BBC in 2013.
97680ed97c: Ambassador Marshall Green recommends spreading “the story of PKI guilt, treachery and brutality”. The telegram, published by the State Department, predates the massacres.
976cbce117: Haig and the nuns “at the roadblock”
Secretary of State Alexander Haig suggests that the four American nuns killed by the National Guard may have run a roadblock. Guardsmen are convicted in 1984.
976d05803d: American military adviser Eric Buckland tells the FBI that a Salvadoran colonel had warned him of a plan against the Jesuits. The information stays hidden for several weeks.
9773b47519: A Million Dollars to Bring Down Mossadegh
According to the CIA's internal history, Director Allen Dulles authorizes the Tehran station to spend a million dollars “in any way” that would bring about Mossadegh's fall.
979449143d: After one of their own is killed, Marines kill 24 civilians, including women and children, in their homes. No prison sentence is handed down.
97c54f69bd: In response to the Khan Shaykhun chemical attack, 59 Tomahawk missiles strike a Syrian air base.
97d5793b0d: Two U.S. military personnel are arrested with tens of thousands of cartridges, suspected of being destined for paramilitaries. Covered by immunity, they are handed over to the United States.
97e148caac: Sudanese spy chief hosted by the CIA
In the midst of the Darfur crisis, the CIA brings Salah Gosh, head of Sudanese intelligence, to Washington to strengthen counterterrorism cooperation, the Los Angeles Times reveals.
9853e0b62f: A 78-day NATO campaign, without a Security Council mandate, under U.S. command and with a majority of U.S. aircraft.
9860e2416b: Ossetia war: alleged U.S. green light

Moscow accuses Washington of having encouraged Saakashvili's offensive, whose army it had trained and armed. Washington denies it and says it warned Tbilisi; the EU's Tagliavini report does not find a green light. The United States repatriates 2,000 Georgian soldiers from Iraq.
98964043e4: U.S. commandos carry out a helicopter-borne ground raid on a village in South Waziristan. Islamabad denounces a violation of its sovereignty and the deaths of civilians.
98b153cd3f: A CIA officer hands Rolando Cubela, a Cuban commander, a syringe pen to kill Castro. The handover takes place in Paris on the day of Kennedy's assassination.
98c90f567a: More than 20,000 American soldiers land to prevent the return to power of Juan Bosch, elected in 1962. Operation Power Pack.
98e172375b: A $325 million drawdown including additional Bradley and Stryker armored vehicles.
98f08fd8a5: The Moroccan opposition leader is abducted in Paris and disappears. French police officers and the Moroccan services are implicated. A CIA role is alleged and Washington has not opened all its files.
9920ad4a88: A car bomb aimed at Sheikh Fadlallah kills more than 80 people. According to Bob Woodward, CIA director William Casey had had it funded by Saudi Arabia.
993bed8b5a: Ambassador Richard Grenell writes to the German government that Washington would reduce intelligence sharing if Huawei took part in 5G.
994a83a163: Two Western hostages killed by a drone
A strike kills American Warren Weinstein and Italian Giovanni Lo Porto, al-Qaeda hostages. Obama apologizes in April 2015.
9985e4395f: Díaz Lanz Air Raid on Havana

Former Cuban air force chief Pedro Luis Díaz Lanz, in exile, flies over Havana from Florida and drops leaflets. Antiaircraft fire and, according to Cuba, fire from the aircraft cause deaths and dozens of injuries. Castro accuses Washington of tolerating these flights.
999ef1fc5a: The army overthrows João Goulart. Ambassador Lincoln Gordon's cables show Washington's active encouragement; Washington recognizes the new regime within hours.
99a8a9fa6f: Washington signs a mutual defense treaty with Chiang Kai-shek during the first Taiwan Strait crisis. It protects the regime until 1979.
99beadaa31: The State Department trains Brazilian judges, prosecutors and police in combating money laundering. A diplomatic cable published by WikiLeaks lists among the participants judge Sérgio Moro, future judge in Lava Jato.
99caf5d931: A cable signed by Hillary Clinton asks the embassy whether the Argentine president takes medication and how she manages stress. Revealed by WikiLeaks in 2010, it leads Clinton to call Kirchner to express regret.
99dc499f54: Washington withdraws from the tomato suspension agreement and imposes anti-dumping duties of about 17%.
99def06780: Ambassador Luce lets it be known that American military orders will go to the factories where Communist unions are losing ground. The CGIL loses its majority at Fiat in 1955.
99ec924eb5: Sleep deprivation, sexual humiliation, a dog: in 2009, Susan Crawford, the official in charge of the military commissions, acknowledges that this detainee was “tortured.”
99fdaa0c6f: After the hostage-taking at the embassy, Carter freezes by decree several billion dollars of Iranian state assets in the United States.
9a30e83967: American weapons paid for by NATO
Trump announces that NATO allies will buy American weapons, including Patriots, to deliver them to Ukraine. The mechanism takes the name PURL.
9a324ce005: American ships bombard Druze militias to support the Lebanese army, making the multinational force a party to the conflict.
9a5dbf86d3: NATO aircraft destroy a bridge on market day: ten civilians killed. Victims sue Germany in court, without success.
9a5dda1b2d: Since 1971, American submarines had been placing taps on a Soviet military cable. Betrayed by Ronald Pelton, the operation is discovered by the Soviets in 1981.
9a62cbe68f: Bombing of the Quỳnh Lập leprosarium
Hanoi accuses US aircraft of repeatedly bombing the Quỳnh Lập leprosarium and killing patients there.
9aaea42335: CIA agents seize tens of thousands of documents from the fallen government to prove Soviet control. They find no evidence of it, according to the CIA's internal history.
9ad0622fbf: Sanctions against Mugabe and his circle
An executive order by George W. Bush freezes the assets of Robert Mugabe and dozens of Zimbabwean officials. The program remains in place until March 2024.
9ad3b4e56c: The Pentagon studies massive bomber strikes, with the option of atomic bombs, to relieve Dien Bien Phu. Eisenhower gives up for lack of British and congressional support.
9ae86275e0: Under pressure from Congress, the White House lifts the freeze on about $391 million in military aid to Ukraine, blocked since July.
9b2f8459b3: American troops occupy Dutch Guiana, in agreement with the Dutch government in exile, to protect the bauxite supply. Listed in Congressional Research Service report R42738.
9b84e7806c: Moscow shuts down the U.S. aid agency, which funded among others the election-monitoring NGO Golos, accusing it of political interference.
9bd792723b: The hearings of the Senate Symington subcommittee reveal that in 1960 Washington secretly pledged to support the Ethiopian army in exchange for Kagnew, and that American advisers support counterinsurgency in Eritrea.
9bde9dbf66: After the Chagai tests, the same sanctions hit Pakistan, already subject to the Pressler Amendment. They are lifted for both countries in September 2001.
9c22e8f411: U.S. forces settle in at al-Tanf, near the Iraqi and Jordanian borders, and impose a 55-km exclusion zone. The garrison, set up without Damascus's consent, blocks the Baghdad-Damascus road.
9c4e81026b: Ronald Reagan vetoes the Comprehensive Anti-Apartheid Act, which imposes sanctions on Pretoria. Congress overrides it on 2 October 1986.
9c5af58c15: The largest package to that date: $3.075 billion including 50 Bradley fighting vehicles and self-propelled howitzers.
9c7f1d609a: Murder of Liu Ziran in Taipei
American Sergeant Robert Reynolds kills Liu Ziran. His acquittal by a court-martial provokes the May 24, 1957 riot against the American embassy.
9c807b6914: Developed with MI5 at a joint workshop, this implant makes Samsung televisions appear to be off while recording conversations in the room. Revealed by WikiLeaks in Vault 7 in March 2017.
9c81993b88: Special forces attack two buildings and kill 21 men, in fact Karzai supporters. Prisoners are beaten. Washington acknowledges the error and pays compensation.
9c927d8ab5: Washington opens Addis Ababa to the EPRDF
After Mengistu's flight, Assistant Secretary of State Herman Cohen, mediator in London, publicly recommends that the EPRDF rebels enter Addis Ababa. They take the capital on 28 May.
9ca6276935: Paul Bremer, head of the Coalition Provisional Authority, bars members of the top four ranks of the Baath Party from the civil service. Tens of thousands of officials, including teachers, are dismissed.
9cc7c37ecf: The day after Maduro's capture, Trump calls Gustavo Petro a cocaine trafficker and says a military operation in Colombia “sounds good.” Bogotá denounces interference.
9cf0accf62: Three atomic tests, X-Ray, Yoke and Zebra, are detonated on Enewetak Atoll, whose inhabitants had been displaced to Ujelang a few months earlier.
9d12186ce2: Niño Guerrero killed in a strike
The head of Tren de Aragua, Héctor “Niño” Guerrero, is killed in a joint US-Venezuelan operation. Trump announces a US air strike.
9d274e3cb7: US justice indicts Colombian businessman Alex Saab for money laundering in a Venezuela-linked corruption network, and the Treasury sanctions him over the CLAP food program.
9d2d275c58: Freeh acknowledges files on independence activists
FBI director Louis Freeh admits before Congress that the Bureau carried out illegal actions against independence activists and contributed to the “carpetas,” political surveillance files.
9d2e7d3c95: The United States strikes Islamic State camps in northwestern Nigeria, in coordination with Abuja, according to Donald Trump and AFRICOM.
9d47052650: Washington terminates the Hungarian tax treaty

The US Treasury gives notice of the end of the 1979 tax treaty with Hungary, which blocks the global minimum tax in the EU. The termination takes effect in January 2023 and makes taxation of flows between the two countries more expensive.
9d4dbe8d87: Funds from the NED, USAID and American foundations back the OK'98 civic campaign, which mobilizes voters against Vladimír Mečiar in the legislative elections.
9d8da881a7: Marines under Major Smedley Butler storm the last Caco stronghold. Several dozen defenders are killed, with no prisoners taken.
9d9afb9306: A $125 million drawdown of anti-aircraft missiles, shells and ammunition.
9da0f946d5: Strikes after the Camp Taji attack

In retaliation for a rocket attack, the United States strikes Kataib Hezbollah sites. The Iraqi army says the strikes killed soldiers, police officers and a civilian, notably at the airport under construction in Karbala.
9dac2537b9: Fellows and volunteers asked to spy
An embassy security officer asks a Fulbright scholar and Peace Corps volunteers to report on Cubans and Venezuelans in Bolivia. The embassy acknowledges a “mistake.”
9dbdbf1991: The Californian subsidiary of the Dutch bank pleads guilty to obstructing a US regulator's examination of its anti-money-laundering system on the Mexican border. It pays about 369 million dollars.
9dc1e81a2f: The president of the national railways, tasked with laying off tens of thousands of railway workers, is found mangled on a track. Novelist Matsumoto Seichō attributes his death to occupation intelligence. The case has never been solved.
9ddc6e70d0: The CIA-funded Free Europe Committee releases from Bavaria thousands of balloons loaded with leaflets (Operation Prospero), then over Hungary and Poland until 1956.
9e031958d0: A military employee recruited by the CIA
The Ministry of State Security announces the arrest of Mr. Zeng, an employee of a military group, recruited in Italy by a CIA agent.
9e1efc32de: A CIA drone kills the al-Qaeda leader on the balcony of a house in Kabul with two Hellfire missiles.
9e38d285f4: Marines abduct Hashim Ibrahim Awad, a disabled civilian, kill him and stage the scene as combat. Several are convicted.
9e696d6f4d: Uday and Qusay Hussein killed in Mosul
Special forces and the 101st Airborne Division besiege a villa and kill Saddam Hussein's two sons, as well as Mustafa, Qusay's 14-year-old son.
9e839ef0c5: Vice President Agnew visits the junta

Spiro Agnew is the first senior Western leader to visit Greece since the 1967 coup. He meets Georgios Papadopoulos and describes military aid to the junta as “of capital importance” for the United States.
9e879bf041: For seven weeks, Strategic Air Command RB-47s secretly overfly the north of the USSR to photograph its bases.
9e8ca1f0cc: Execution of SS Guards at Dachau
During the liberation of the camp, American soldiers kill SS guards who had surrendered. An Army inquiry is closed without action.
9e907042d8: After MacArthur's order to burn the towns near the Yalu, B-29s drop incendiary bombs on Sinuiju. Much of the town is destroyed.
9ecb821f0e: Oliver North's network builds a secret airstrip in Costa Rica to resupply the Contras of the southern front.
9ece6ecf14: Pressure on the Shah Through Princess Ashraf
The CIA and MI6 persuade the Shah's twin sister to return to Tehran to convince her brother to sign Mossadegh's dismissal.
9ef3d9a10a: U.S. bombers strike the village of Granai. The Afghan government counts about 140 civilian dead; the military admits “errors.”
9ef4b9069c: The Pentagon announces $125 million in aid under the USAI, including two armed patrol boats, radars and medical equipment.
9f1d8c7962: Kaspersky discovers software from the Flame family that steals banking credentials, mainly in Lebanon. Its attribution remains a hypothesis.
9f27089362: With Washington's backing, Guaidó's Assembly appoints a new board for Citgo, PDVSA's US subsidiary, depriving Caracas of its main foreign asset.
9f7e5cc125: At Washington's urging, the Organization of American States excludes the Cuban government. Only six countries abstain.
9fa9189a53: In the 1950s, according to Finnish historians drawing on archives, American funds, including from the CIA, support the anti-communist wing of the Social Democratic Party and its press against the communists.
9fec8bfa31: The Greek junta overthrows the Cypriot president, then Turkey invades the island. Kissinger is accused of having let it happen. A direct American role is not proven.
a008ed1e3d: In early January 1951, B-29s launch massive incendiary raids on Pyongyang. They are part of the systematic destruction of the cities of the North.
a059b64b7c: Operation Phantom Fury razes much of the city. The main hospital is seized at the very start of the assault.
a0814dbb86: During these large-scale exercises, the US Navy simulates the invasion of a fictional island, “Amber and the Amberdines”, which the Grenadian government interprets as a rehearsal against Grenada.
a094e3ca30: Just before the ceasefire, the US military again strikes military targets on Kharg Island, the heart of Iranian oil exports.
a096c02754: Trump vetoes resolution on the Yemen war
Trump vetoes the congressional resolution that ordered an end to military support for the Saudi coalition, the first passed under the War Powers Act.
a09ed0a4ed: The CIA has Pasternak's banned novel printed and hands out copies to Soviet visitors at the Brussels World's Fair. Documents declassified in 2014.
a0d112aecf: American aircraft and ships transport hundreds of thousands of Kuomintang soldiers to the north and Manchuria, to get ahead of the Communists after the Japanese surrender.
a0dfd6addd: A $175 million drawdown of HIMARS ammunition and air defense.
a0e0857d5d: Amnesty records some fifty stopovers at Shannon by aircraft used by the CIA for renditions. A 2007 cable published by WikiLeaks shows Minister Dermot Ahern convinced that at least three such flights touched Ireland.
a0fb997e9b: Moscow sees it as a U.S. operation. NGOs received funds from the United States and the Soros foundation; no orchestration is demonstrated.
a0ffe8ad1c: A U.S. raid and air strikes kill about 90 civilians according to the UN, including about sixty children. The military first denied it, then acknowledged 33 civilian deaths.
a11a099699: After the second Dutch “police action”, Washington suspends aid intended for the Dutch East Indies and threatens to cut off Marshall Plan aid to the Netherlands if they do not accept Indonesian independence.
a12120a967: After the attack on Saudi Abqaiq facilities, a US cyber operation targets Iran's ability to spread its propaganda, according to Reuters.
a1b02f42d2: The first software designed to destroy physical equipment: it sabotages Iranian centrifuges. The New York Times attributes it to the U.S.-Israeli operation “Olympic Games.”
a1ceeb8212: An American satellite detects a double flash, probably an Israeli-South African nuclear test. A White House panel concludes it was a false signal; declassified documents show internal doubts.
a1de904f21: On the day of Aristide's departure, Marines land in Port-au-Prince, leading an interim multinational force, before MINUSTAH takes over in June.
a1e0638e2e: According to Zelensky, Trump approves granting Ukraine licenses to produce Patriot missiles. The White House has not publicly confirmed it.
a1edaa1e6d: A bomb targets Contra leader Edén Pastora, who had broken with the CIA, at a press conference and kills several people, including journalists. Journalists suspected the CIA. Nothing has been proven.
a1ff8ba076: According to Cuban counterintelligence, a Habana Libre hotel employee recruited by networks linked to the CIA was to pour a cyanide capsule into Castro's milkshake. The capsule reportedly stuck to the freezer.
a2051357d9: Biden signs an executive order that restricts US investment in semiconductors, quantum and AI in China.
a21fcad4a0: General Herbert Norman Schwarzkopf, former instructor of the Iranian gendarmerie, comes to persuade the Shah to sign the decrees appointing Fazlollah Zahedi in place of Mossadegh.
a229c56b28: Georgios Papadopoulos, head of the junta, had long-standing ties with the CIA. A direct American role in the putsch is not proven. Bill Clinton expresses regret in 1999 for the support given to the dictatorship.
a23ff505dd: George W. Bush says that Iraq could use drones to spread chemical or biological weapons, including against the United States. The Air Force had already disputed this analysis.
a25b7012a4: Provided for by the 1915 convention, the gendarmerie is commanded by Marine officers. It administers the corvée and fights the Cacos, before becoming the Garde d'Haïti.
a261e6f13d: In Operation Red Dawn, soldiers of the 4th Infantry Division and special forces capture Saddam Hussein in an underground hideout near Tikrit. He remains in U.S. military custody.
a27bc14a4a: To retake the city during the Tet Offensive, artillery, aircraft and Marines destroy much of Huế and its citadel. Thousands of civilians die, also victims of the massacre committed by the communist side.
a27fb8dbff: Marines surrounded by the Sandinistas at Quilalí are resupplied and evacuated by air. Pilot Christian Schilt receives the Medal of Honor.
a2b688156b: Truman commits air and naval forces, then ground troops on June 30, under a UN mandate. About 1.8 million Americans will serve in the war.
a2c988ec13: Eisenhower Refuses Any Aid to Mossadegh
Eisenhower replies to Mossadegh that no economic aid will be granted until the oil dispute is settled. The letter is made public in July to weaken the government.
a2d787c488: Orlando Bosch and other exiles found the Coordination of United Revolutionary Organizations, which claims dozens of attacks against Cuban interests. Declassified archives show that the CIA and the FBI were aware of them.
a2f1aa39a2: The Marshall Plan administration funds films, exhibitions, trains and brochures to promote the American model and combat Communist influence in Europe.
a30e9a78e9: For the third anniversary of the 2020 election, the Treasury sanctions the national airline Belavia and several entities and individuals close to Lukashenko.
a3289716fb: Washington imposes anti-dumping and countervailing duties of up to about 20% and 27% on black table olives from Spain. In 2021, the WTO finds part of these duties contrary to its rules; they remain in place.
a3ac5447d3: CIA Pilot Shot Down at Ambon
Pilot Allen Pope, who was bombing targets for the Permesta rebels, is shot down over Ambon. His capture exposes the American role and Washington drops the rebellion.
a3d0a5f60f: Before the presidential runoff, the White House publicly asks Aristide not to return and Barack Obama calls South African President Jacob Zuma.
a3d1f4bbf6: Officers kill President Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and his family. Journalist Lawrence Lifschultz claims the American embassy was in contact with the plotters. Washington denies any role.
a3e7680d82: Executive order on 40% tariffs on Brazil
Trump declares a national emergency and imposes an additional 40% tariff on Brazilian goods, citing the prosecution of Jair Bolsonaro.
a3f05c500f: The State Department offers up to $15 million for information leading to Maduro's arrest, and $10 million for other officials.
a406e7fcae: Biden signs the Additional Ukraine Supplemental Appropriations Act, which opens about $40 billion, about $20 billion of it for defense.
a418df0762: Defence Minister Botelho Moniz tries to remove Salazar in order to change colonial policy. Historians believe that the Kennedy administration, hostile to that policy, was ready to discreetly support this change; the American role is not established.
a4526a8ab1: The Castillo Armas regime creates a committee that files tens of thousands of suspects and has thousands of people arrested. Historians describe CIA support for this filing.
a47904cd7f: Justice Minister Beatrice Ask confirms that the American embassy has carried out since 2000 secret surveillance of individuals around its premises, unknown to the Swedish authorities. A prosecutor opens an investigation.
a48d224d82: Marco Rubio announces that El Salvador agrees to imprison, for a fee, people deported from the United States, including criminals with US citizenship.
a4941cf260: After the Sabra and Shatila massacres, some 1,200 Marines return to Beirut in a new multinational force. They remain until February 1984. Listed in Congressional Research Service report R42738.
a49a019d30: A military coup prepared by the CIA with Iyad Allawi's Iraqi National Accord is uncovered. Dozens of officers are arrested and executed.
a4b165f3ae: A $325 million drawdown of HIMARS ammunition, shells and anti-tank missiles.
a4b2c3142d: The destroyer USS DeHaven fires on a refugee camp by the sea near Pohang, at the army's request. The Truth and Reconciliation Commission concludes in 2008 that 100 to 200 civilians died.
a4d2362d42: Rafael Trujillo joins the National Guard and becomes an officer under the occupation. Trained and promoted by the Marines, he relies on this force to seize power in 1930.
a4f14baee8: According to the New York Times (2025), a US cell provides Ukraine every day with coordinates of Russian targets and helps plan its offensives.
a4f2e9d7ff: The CIA funds the Liberal Democratic Party and some of its candidates from the late 1950s. The State Department acknowledged it in 2006 in its diplomatic records (FRUS).
a51b2280fc: Washington places the Sinaloa cartel, Tren de Aragua and other groups on the list of terrorist organizations, a legal basis later invoked for military strikes.
a521d670ca: Swede Mehdi Ghezali, arrested in Pakistan, is held without trial for 930 days at Guantánamo, then released in July 2004 without charges. He says he suffered cold, noise and permanent light.
a5226a1370: During his surprise visit to Kyiv, Biden announces new aid; the Pentagon details a $460 million drawdown of ammunition.
a5411b079a: The United States delivers aid to the border to force Maduro's blockade. A truck burns; the New York Times shows the fire came from an opposition protester's Molotov cocktail.
a552e6bef3: Kenya is among the countries whose mobile call metadata the NSA collects under the MYSTIC program. Revealed by The Intercept in May 2014.
a55c0ffa62: During the evacuation, a drone kills aid worker Zemari Ahmadi and nine members of his family, including seven children. The Pentagon acknowledges a “tragic mistake,” with no punishment.
a583b604e8: After the downing of a US drone, Cyber Command attacks missile control systems and an Iranian intelligence database, according to officials cited by the press.
a5985635ff: Arrested in Dar es Salaam, this Yemeni is transferred to Djibouti and then to secret CIA prisons. He is sent back to Yemen in 2005 without charge, according to Amnesty International.
a5c2a6eac6: Radio Liberty broadcasts to the Baltic states
Radio Liberty, funded by Congress, launches programmes in Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian, merged in 1983 into a Baltic service. The broadcasts end in 2004.
a5c4bf7a07: Troop transit to Iraq via Shannon

Tens of thousands of American soldiers transit through Shannon airport to Iraq. In 2003, the High Court finds that the State thereby violates the law of neutrality (Hague Convention), without ordering it to stop.
a5f1c62776: US strikes and a commando operation capture the Venezuelan president, transferred to New York to be tried for drug trafficking.
a5fdaee7bc: Washington launches a series of military exercises in Kuwait after Iraq refuses to recognize the new border and to cooperate with UN inspectors. Listed in Congressional Research Service report R42738.
a6073b21af: According to declassified archives, Henry Kissinger supports the Moroccan claim to Spanish Sahara during the Green March. The Madrid Accords of 14 November divide the territory between Morocco and Mauritania, without the Sahrawis.
a6168a4322: GCHQ fake internet cafés at the London G20

British intelligence, an ally of the NSA, sets up fake internet cafés, hacks BlackBerrys and targets in particular the Turkish and South African delegations during the 2009 G20 meetings. Revealed by The Guardian in June 2013.
a62f75d3b9: Biden signs the $95 billion national security package, including $60.8 billion for Ukraine, and immediately announces a $1 billion drawdown.
a6498ba28d: A US Army study identifies 35 sites contaminated with hydrocarbons and heavy metals in the soil and groundwater of Terceira island around the Lajes base. The Portuguese laboratory LNEC confirms the pollution in 2009.
a65b325829: The Colombian army creates intelligence networks on the advice of a Pentagon and CIA team. Human Rights Watch shows in 1996 that they are used for assassinations with paramilitaries.
a670ece411: “The price is worth it”: Madeleine Albright
Asked about the estimated death of half a million Iraqi children under the embargo, the UN ambassador replies that “the price is worth it”. That figure from the time has since been contested.
a69b51860a: The National Endowment for Democracy increases its grants to Venezuelan groups, including unions and business organizations that will lead the 2002 coup. The amounts were made public by the NED.
a69bfa1dae: The CIA-funded Free Europe Press launches by balloon towards Poland brochures repeating Józef Świło's revelations about the political police.
a6aa3419a2: The CIA trains the Cuban exiles of the future Brigade 2506 at a secret base in Guatemala, with President Ydígoras's agreement.
a6baec024b: North Korea relisted as a terrorist state
Trump puts North Korea back on the list of state sponsors of terrorism, citing in particular the assassination of Kim Jong-nam.
a6c7e6a386: CIA aircraft carrying detainees to Guantánamo fly over the Azores and stop over at Porto or Ponta Delgada. After MEP Ana Gomes refers the matter to it, the prosecutor's office opens an investigation in February 2007, closed in 2009 for lack of evidence.
a6f4a84203: Nixon and Médici against Allende and Castro
A declassified memorandum records that Nixon and Brazilian dictator Médici discuss cooperating to overthrow Allende and Castro. Nixon offers “discreet” help.
a71337eabc: Ferdinand Marcos proclaims martial law. Informed in advance, the Nixon administration does not oppose it and maintains military aid, in exchange for the security of the Clark and Subic bases.
a71f32c29d: A Trump executive order declares a national emergency targeting Cuba and threatens tariffs on countries that supply it with oil.
a72f1fcc58: U-2 Shot Down Over the USSR
Francis Gary Powers's spy plane is shot down. Washington first denies, then acknowledges the overflights. The Paris summit fails.
a7432d3ec4: Pressure against Italy's Belt and Road participation
The White House publicly warns Rome against joining the Belt and Road Initiative, signed on 23 March 2019. Italy, the only G7 country to have joined, withdraws at the end of 2023.
a76b499a40: After Juan Orta's failure, Roselli and Trafficante entrust the pills to the exile Tony Varona, who says he has a contact in a restaurant frequented by Castro. The Bay of Pigs failure ends the project, according to the Church Committee.
a76c93584f: AEFREEMAN programme for the Baltic states
The CIA funds Baltic exile organisations to “harass” the Soviet regime. The Estonian component AEROOT/AEBASIN (1953-1960) also provides for the infiltration of agents. Files declassified.
a781f57ce1: According to Bob Woodward in the Washington Post in 1987, the CIA supplies Iran with partly falsified intelligence on the Iraqi army, while briefing Iraq.
a79a2dc1d3: Iraqi National Congress, created with the CIA
The exiled opposition founds Ahmed Chalabi's Iraqi National Congress. The CIA funds the operation through the public relations firm Rendon Group, according to ABC News and New Yorker investigations.
a7ab8957d8: After denying it, the Pentagon acknowledges in November 2005 that it used white phosphorus as a weapon against fighters in Fallujah. Its use near civilians is denounced.
a7bfb05df9: According to Reuters (2024), the US military spreads messages disparaging the Chinese Sinovac vaccine through fake accounts, in the midst of the pandemic.
a7ccb4938d: Charlie Company kills between 347 and 504 civilians. Lieutenant William Calley is the only one convicted, and later has his sentence reduced.
a7d2625d3d: Bombing of the Red River dikes
Hanoi accuses Washington of deliberately targeting the dikes to cause flooding. The American government speaks of accidental damage.
a80bf464fb: Sabotage of the Puerto Sandino pipeline
CIA commandos sabotage the Puerto Sandino undersea oil pipeline. The Contras claim the attack.
a824d9e2c4: The US Air Force seeds clouds to prolong the monsoon over the Ho Chi Minh Trail until 1972. Revealed in 1971, it leads to the 1977 ENMOD convention.
a82946dddb: A strike requested by Afghan forces kills about ten civilians, including children. Karzai subsequently bars his troops from requesting air strikes.
a855a0f4ea: Operation Peter Pan and a False Rumor

More than 14,000 Cuban children are sent alone to the United States from 1960 to 1962, with American visa waivers. Radio Swan spreads the false rumor that the state will strip parents of authority over their children.
a868199690: The destroyer Lassen passes within 12 miles of an artificial Chinese reef. It is the first “freedom of navigation” patrol near China's artificial islands.
a87728b2b0: Strike on the village of Azizi
Coalition strikes on the village of Azizi, targeting Taliban, kill dozens of civilians according to Afghan authorities.
a8925649b5: A U-2 spy plane photographs Soviet missile launch sites. The overflights multiply. On October 27, a U-2 is shot down over Oriente and its pilot Rudolf Anderson is killed.
a8a775880c: A U.S. drone kills the leader of the Afghan Taliban on a road in Balochistan, the first strike outside the tribal areas.
a8cce8e6c2: On the day of Ortega's inauguration, Washington sanctions six officials and restricts visas for more than 100 elected officials and judges.
a8d334e248: Strike on the “tall man” of Zhawar Kili

A CIA Predator kills three men, including one named Daraz Khan, mistaken for bin Laden because of his height. They were collecting scrap metal, according to their relatives. The Pentagon judges the target “appropriate” while admitting it did not know who he was.
a8d4f800af: After Houthi attacks in the Red Sea, the United States and the United Kingdom bomb targets in Yemen, the first of a long series.
a8ebd1a4e3: During the Battle of Anzio, Allied bombers, American according to most accounts, hit the papal properties of Castel Gandolfo where thousands of refugees are sheltering. Hundreds of civilians are killed. The Holy See protests.
a91385c2bd: The State Department bans the former European commissioner and other platform regulation figures from receiving visas, accused of “censorship” by Washington.
a91acc0d75: A NATO bomb intended for a barracks lands on a residential neighborhood in Surdulica and kills about twenty civilians.
a921a4f638: Washington blocks a draft asking Israel to give up the Har Homa settlement in East Jerusalem.
a92f485b88: CIA agents at the Turkish border
According to the New York Times, CIA agents operate in southern Turkey to decide which Syrian rebel groups receive the weapons paid for by Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Qatar.
a949cc9002: “Third” countries, including Denmark and Germany, let the NSA install its equipment on their fiber-optic cables; the program costs $170 million from 2011 to 2013. Revealed by Information and The Intercept in June 2014.
a95f43504f: Refusal to jam Radio Mille Collines
A Pentagon memo judges jamming RTLM, which calls for massacres, too costly and contrary to freedom of the airwaves. Washington gives it up, according to declassified documents.
a961db9d51: Visas revoked over the Mais Médicos program
The State Department revokes the visas of Brazilian officials linked to the program that had brought in Cuban doctors.
a96bec0f30: The United States deploys nuclear weapons in Taiwan from 1958 to 1974, including Matador missiles at Tainan, according to a declassified Pentagon history.
a9bab5d41b: The Italian group UniCredit pays about $1.3 billion for violations of sanctions on Iran and other countries.
a9feca7b18: Four tests, including George, the first thermonuclear fusion experiment, contaminate the islets of Enewetak Atoll.
aa01638e16: According to the Washington Post, a second strike kills two survivors of the first attack. The White House confirms the strike and defends it; legal experts speak of a war crime.
aa106300e3: Marine aircraft dive-bomb the Sandinistas besieging Ocotal. Nicaraguan casualties, civilians included, number in the dozens or hundreds depending on the source.
aa528e188b: Evo Morales's plane blocked in Vienna
Suspected of carrying Edward Snowden, the Bolivian presidential plane is denied overflight by France, Spain, Italy and Portugal. Bolivia denounces U.S. pressure.
aa65c38cbd: About 300 paratroopers of the 173rd Brigade begin training the Ukrainian national guard at Yavoriv, as part of Operation Fearless Guardian.
aa6b9d2ac8: The former Venezuelan industry minister is arrested in a joint operation by US and Venezuelan intelligence, according to a US official. He is expelled to the United States in May 2026.
aa9626bee1: Trump announces a new strike on a vessel described as a drug-trafficking boat linked to Venezuela: three dead. No public evidence is provided.
aa9c5410d5: Washington restricts access to financing for Rosneft, Novatek, Gazprombank and VEB, then extends the measures after the downing of flight MH17.
aaae5075d7: The United States and Jordan strike more than 35 Islamic State targets in Syria, in retaliation for the Palmyra ambush that killed two US soldiers and an interpreter in December.
aaaec24e8c: The German bank is penalized for violating U.S. embargoes against Iran and Sudan and for anti-money-laundering failures.
aabbd81fbb: Washington suspends its oil deliveries to force an end to wolfram sales to Germany. The Spanish economy is paralysed; the May 1944 agreement reduces these exports and restores deliveries.
ab093ef940: Washington imposes on the Cuban Constitution a U.S. right of intervention and the cession of naval bases, as a condition for withdrawing its troops.
ab16debd1c: Arrest of the head of Pilatus Bank

Ali Sadr Hashemi Nejad, chairman of the Maltese bank Pilatus, is arrested near Washington for circumventing sanctions against Iran. The Maltese regulator immediately removes him from the bank's management.
ab604e2a61: Eisenhower approves a plan to isolate Nasser, reduce aid to Egypt and consider covert actions, according to State Department archives.
ab76bc3371: Carter signs a directive authorizing covert aid to opponents of the communist regime in Kabul, six months before the Soviet intervention. Brzezinski confirmed it in 1998.
aba8eb2d0b: The Treasury sanctions seven officials, including Igor Sechin (Rosneft) and Sergey Chemezov (Rostec), and seventeen companies linked to Putin's entourage. Commerce restricts sensitive exports.
abc3f37305: Veto on the occupation of the territories
Washington blocks a draft deploring the continued Israeli occupation of the territories conquered in 1967 and calling for a solution taking into account the rights of the Palestinians.
abc51e1959: Daimler pays $185 million under the FCPA
The German automaker settles for $185 million over bribes paid in some twenty countries.
abe3aed5a8: Washington obtains from the Libyan monarchy the use of Wheelus air base, near Tripoli, in return for financial aid. The base is used for U.S. Air Force training until its evacuation, demanded by Gaddafi, in June 1970.
ac0c80e904: Support for the Khmer Rouge's UN seat
After the Vietnamese invasion, Washington votes for the Khmer Rouge's Democratic Kampuchea to keep Cambodia's seat at the UN, then for the coalition they dominate, until 1991.
ac12db2c5c: First raid ordered by Trump: the Navy SEAL assault, backed by air strikes, kills civilians, including Nawar al-Awlaki, 8, a U.S. citizen. A Navy SEAL is killed by fighters.
ac162d0c49: A Trump executive order renames the Gulf of Mexico the “Gulf of America” in federal documents; the AP is barred from events for keeping the old name.
ac45f96efe: Clinton's envoy, Bill Richardson, arranges the meeting between Mobutu and Kabila on a South African ship and presses the marshal to step down. Mobutu flees Kinshasa on 16 May.
ac64686847: Strike on a funeral at Makeen

A drone strikes the funeral of a fighter; more than 60 dead according to the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, many of them civilians. This tactic of following up with a second strike on gatherings is documented.
ac728781af: About 1,300 U.S. soldiers, including special forces, are deployed against Abu Sayyaf during exercise Balikatan 02-1. A special operations task force remains in the south until 2015.
ac748e7f4d: Commerce extends the Entity List to any company 50% owned by a listed entity. The rule is suspended for a year in November after a trade truce.
ac76828490: Argentine frigate seized by a vulture fund
At the request of NML Capital, a fund of U.S. billionaire Paul Singer, a Ghanaian court impounds the three-masted ARA Libertad. The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea orders its release.
ac98fa794a: General Westmoreland prepares the delivery of nuclear weapons to South Vietnam. The plan is abandoned in February 1968 after leaks. Declassified cables, revealed in 2018, confirm it.
aca42ba9dd: Agreement creating the Pine Gap base

Australia and the United States sign the agreement creating a spy satellite control station near Alice Springs, linked to the CIA. Its true function remains hidden from the Australian Parliament for a long time.
aca660dc97: The CIA destroys 92 recordings of interrogations of Abu Zubaydah and al-Nashiri on the orders of Jose Rodriguez. No prosecution is brought.
aca8030ccb: George W. Bush declares that Taylor must leave power. Pressed by Washington and surrounded by rebels, he goes into exile in Nigeria on August 11, while Marines briefly land in Monrovia.
acb44080f7: The Soacha scandal reveals the killing of civilians dressed up as guerrillas; the JEP counts 6,402 victims from 2002 to 2008. NGOs show that units funded by Washington took part.
acd387acb5: Washington bans all arms sales to Venezuela, deemed uncooperative on counterterrorism, and also blocks the sale of Spanish and Brazilian aircraft containing U.S. components.
acdad378f9: Tibetan Guerrillas Armed by the CIA
The CIA parachutes into Tibet the first Tibetans trained on Saipan. Drops of agents and arms continue until the mid-1960s (ST CIRCUS program).
acee63f92a: Before entering the war, Washington authorizes the recruitment of resigned military pilots for the American Volunteer Group, which fights Japan on behalf of China.
acf76325b2: Tilanne magazine funded by the CIA
Founded by former Finnish communists, this left-wing magazine appears from 1961 to 1967. It is partly funded by the Congress for Cultural Freedom, whose secret backer was the CIA.
acfecd428d: Dozens of special forces members are flown by helicopter near Raqqa to free Islamic State hostages, including James Foley. The hostages are not there. The Pentagon reveals the raid in August.
ad0aa332a3: Doctors of the U.S. Public Health Service deliberately infect more than 1,300 prisoners, soldiers and mental patients (1946–1948). Washington apologizes in 2010.
ad0d1405fb: Under General Keith Alexander, the NSA collects nearly all calls, text messages and emails in Iraq through a program called Real Time Regional Gateway, according to the Washington Post.
ad12a0f3f2: President Arosemena breaks with Havana under army pressure, at the end of a campaign that Philip Agee attributes to the CIA.
ad25f435d3: Washington blocks a draft declaring the construction of the wall in the West Bank illegal. The General Assembly then refers the matter to the International Court of Justice.
ad376cd8ed: Ilopango, base of the North network
Oliver North's network uses Ilopango military airport to resupply the Contras, with former CIA agent Félix Rodríguez. The Iran-Contra investigations establish this.
ad4c7b3c62: A federal judge in Delaware approves the auction sale of Citgo's parent company to Amber Energy, linked to the Elliott fund, to pay Venezuela's creditors.
ad539e1880: According to former ambassador Daniel Patrick Moynihan, the CIA funds the Congress Party against the elected Communist government of Kerala, dismissed by New Delhi in 1959.
ad98b49e82: Civilian aircraft under contract to the U.S. military take off from Ouagadougou to monitor the Sahel. The Washington Post reveals in 2012 this program launched in 2007.
adb1aaa15d: The 2023 appropriations law signed by Biden includes about $45 billion for Ukraine and NATO, a large share of it military aid.
adb2423214: Scott Bessent announces that the US Treasury is directly buying pesos to support the Argentine currency, two weeks before the midterm elections.
adcbd48a64: A CIA aircraft sent to pick up an agent is shot down over Manchuria. John Downey and Richard Fecteau are held for twenty years; Washington acknowledges only in 1973 that they worked for the CIA.
adf1d3d8bb: After Noriega annuls the election, Bush sends a brigade of about 1,900 soldiers to reinforce the some 11,000 American military personnel already there. Listed in Congressional Research Service report R42738.
ae20a4fd7e: The Supreme Court declines to hear the appeals of Bikini and Enewetak, which sought the compensation awarded by the Nuclear Claims Tribunal, more than $2 billion never paid.
ae212faac6: With A-37s and helicopters supplied by Washington, the army bombs areas held by the FMLN. Americas Watch documents civilian casualties.
ae30a86afc: The American company Freeport Sulphur signs with Suharto's regime the first foreign mining contract, for the Ertsberg mountain, two years before the contested 1969 vote on Papua's status.
ae4eed6d5a: An international loan places Liberia's customs under the authority of an American general receiver, assisted by European receivers. Washington thus controls the state's main source of revenue.
ae8750cf7a: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, funded by Congress, launches an Arabic-language radio station aimed at Iraqis, as part of the regime change policy.
aed301ff17: Ambassador George Glass tells Expresso that Portugal must choose between its allies and China, notably over 5G and the port of Sines. Minister Santos Silva replies that Lisbon decides alone.
aedf4c9e99: Ahmed Abdi Godane killed in a strike
A U.S. air strike near Barawe kills the al-Shabaab leader. The Pentagon confirms his death a few days later.
aef98da7dc: The bank settles US prosecutions for corruption in Libya and Libor manipulation.
af16d2ffce: A raid to capture Aidid's lieutenants turns into urban combat; 18 American soldiers and several hundred Somalis, many of them civilians, are killed.
af21b2e3a8: An exit poll by Penn, Schoen & Berland conducted with Súmate announces Chávez's defeat. The recall referendum gives him 59%; international observers validate the result.
af6165d43b: After the attack on the Abqaiq facilities, Washington sends troops, Patriot batteries and a THAAD system to Saudi Arabia. Listed in Congressional Research Service report R42738.
af61847b0e: An uprising of Taliban prisoners is crushed by the Northern Alliance and U.S. strikes. Hundreds of prisoners die; Amnesty calls for an investigation that was never opened.
af676f1321: Nixon's blank check to the Shah
On a visit to Tehran, Nixon and Kissinger authorize the Shah to buy any American conventional weapon. Iran becomes the top customer of the American arms industry.
afc0fad4f7: Trump imposes a 10% baseline tariff on almost all countries and higher “reciprocal” rates, up to 50% for Lesotho, before suspending them for 90 days.
afc2f805c7: Colin Powell presents to the Security Council “evidence” of weapons of mass destruction, including mobile labs described by the source “Curveball.” No weapons are found; Powell has called it a “blot.”
afcfe0ea07: The transport operators resume the strike in late July 1973 and hold it until the coup. Private groups funded by the CIA support it, according to the Church Committee.
afda21e96d: Strike on a sports complex in Lamerd
According to the UN fact-finding mission, a US strike scatters tungsten pellets over a sports complex and a residential neighborhood in Lamerd: 22 civilians killed. Washington rejects these findings.
b0059de764: According to the New York Times, Trump signed a directive authorizing the military to act against cartels designated as terrorist. Claudia Sheinbaum rules out any intervention on Mexican soil.
b03bb7a912: American aircraft carry out daytime raids in the Allied campaign against Hamburg, largely British, which causes a firestorm and tens of thousands of deaths.
b03cc7a6ae: Dependent on American aid, revolutionary Bolivia adopts a petroleum code drafted by an American law firm, which reopens the sector to foreign companies.
b08abe63f5: Two Iraqis thrown into the Tigris
Soldiers force two Iraqis to jump into the Tigris; one, Zaidoun Fadhil, drowns according to his family. In 2005, a sergeant is convicted of assault but acquitted of involuntary manslaughter.
b0ac8a3ae8: Washington deploys tactical nuclear weapons in South Korea, despite the armistice article banning the introduction of new armaments. They remain there until 1991.
b0d9730224: The State Department says Panama has agreed to let US government ships pass for free. The Canal Authority and President Mulino deny it.
b0efaf9554: Mas'ud handed over to the United States

Abducted from his home in Tripoli by a militia, Abu Agila Mas'ud is handed over to Washington to stand trial. Libya has no extradition treaty with the United States; Libyans denounce an illegal transfer.
b0f638ea41: Documents reveal that the Pentagon continued to train the Kopassus special forces, through the JCET program, despite the congressional ban. The Pentagon acknowledges it.
b11f2fd85f: CENTCOM and the Saudi air force strike Popular Mobilization Forces sites in several Iraqi provinces: at least 20 fighters killed. Baghdad denounces a violation of its sovereignty.
b123d55285: After the Pokhran II nuclear tests, Clinton applies the Glenn Amendment: end of non-humanitarian aid, veto on international loans, ban on military sales.
b135c235c8: Thousands of U.S. soldiers arrive after the earthquake and take control of the airport. Doctors Without Borders and several governments complain of diverted humanitarian flights.
b13dac4cd0: Washington bans cruise stops and group educational travel to Cuba, the main source of American visitors.
b142b47e72: The minister-president of Hesse reveals a paramilitary group of former soldiers, funded by American services, that kept lists of Social Democratic leaders to be eliminated in the event of an invasion.
b145b85601: Discovered by the Hungarian lab CrySyS, this code, close to Stuxnet, steals industrial data, mainly in Iran. Its attribution to the same authors remains a hypothesis.
b153ae1298: Marines board the Iranian tanker Celestial Sea in the Gulf of Oman and force it to change course. The blockade has by then diverted 91 ships and immobilized four.
b17f1b4f74: The United States bombs Afghanistan and backs the Northern Alliance to overthrow the Taliban. The war lasts twenty years.
b19f82cfdd: Washington forces Seoul to give up the purchase of a French reprocessing plant, threatening the alliance and aid. Park Chung-hee has to put his secret nuclear weapons program on hold.
b1a637d59d: In reprisal for the La Belle bombing, American aircraft bomb Tripoli and Benghazi. Dozens dead, including civilians. The UN General Assembly condemns it.
b1be9bbe72: American troops remain in Bosnia within the NATO stabilization force that succeeds IFOR. Listed in Congressional Research Service report R42738.
b1d5e385c9: Held by the U.S. military, Saddam Hussein is handed over to the Iraqi authorities a few hours before his hanging, after his conviction for the Dujail massacre. A video shows insults hurled by the executioners.
b1e292af0d: Pete Hegseth announces Operation “Southern Spear” against “narco-terrorists”; the aircraft carrier Gerald R. Ford arrives in the Caribbean a few days later.
b210970808: Congress bans all arms sales to both sides in the civil war. The legal Republican government can no longer arm itself in the United States, while Germany and Italy arm Franco. Roosevelt confirms the embargo on 1 May 1937.
b21f001fec: BURMA Act: aid to opponents of the junta
Included in the defense budget, the law authorizes non-lethal aid to the National Unity Government in exile and to armed groups opposing the junta.
b23048605d: Executive Order 14071 bans all new US investment in Russia. Sberbank and Alfa-Bank are blocked, along with Vladimir Putin's daughters.
b230d39511: At the peak in 2007, the army holds more than 20,000 Iraqis, most without charge or trial, mainly at Camp Bucca. Several future Islamic State leaders passed through.
b24dc7b09c: Zelensky unveils the first F-16s delivered by European allies with Washington's authorization and flown by Ukrainians trained in the United States.
b2592bf835: Musk backs Georgescu against Romanian justice

Elon Musk, then a Trump adviser at DOGE, calls the exclusion of Călin Georgescu from the presidential race “crazy” and calls the president of the Constitutional Court a “tyrant”. Clashes break out in Bucharest after the exclusion.
b28c544148: Blackwater in the JSOC secret program
The Nation reports that Blackwater employees take part in Karachi in a strike and capture program of the Joint Special Operations Command. The company denies it.
b2965cfcbc: A bomb explodes at the Meliá Cohiba hotel, the start of a series against tourism. In 1998, Posada Carriles tells the New York Times he organized them with exiles' money. Cuba accuses Washington of protecting him; no American government role is established.
b2983aeb3b: A B-52 carpet of bombs razes this working-class district of Hanoi. About 280 residents are killed.
b2b4f09ea6: Law to force the sale of TikTok
Biden signs a law that requires ByteDance to divest TikTok or face a ban in the United States.
b2bf4ffbbb: B-29s drop incendiary bombs on Kobe. Thousands of civilians are killed and hundreds of thousands lose their homes.
b2c03c3c34: A $600 million drawdown of HIMARS ammunition, shells and demining equipment.
b2ce00385f: Washington cuts Cuba off from Venezuelan oil
After Nicolás Maduro's capture, Trump announces there will be “no more oil or money” for Cuba and calls on Havana to make a deal. Shortages and power cuts worsen.
b2dc51b89c: The Coast Guard and the Southern Spear force seize the tanker Olina, the fifth vessel taken under the “quarantine” imposed on Venezuelan oil.
b2f78b9d8d: A Guantánamo detainee in exchange for a meeting
According to cables published by WikiLeaks, American diplomats link a meeting with Obama to Slovenia taking in a Guantánamo detainee. Ljubljana denied any bargaining.
b319082ea9: AIDS workshops used to recruit in Cuba
According to the AP (2014), a USAID program sends young Latin Americans to Cuba under cover of HIV prevention workshops to identify future opposition figures.
b31de02d5e: The army overthrows Isabel Perón. Washington, informed in advance, quickly recognizes the junta, which causes thousands of disappearances.
b32f170019: Embassy demands an end to DEI policies
The American embassy asks French companies that supply the federal government to certify within five days that they have no diversity programme. Paris denounces “unacceptable” interference.
b332451ac5: Ambassador John Muccio informs the State Department that the army will fire on refugees approaching American lines. His letter, found in 2006, was not cited by the official inquiry.
b3330e3859: After the December 2025 strikes, the Pentagon deploys about 200 military personnel to train Nigerian forces fighting Boko Haram and the Islamic State.
b36201e4a6: The NSA's TAO unit penetrates the management site of the consortium for the cable linking Marseille to Southeast Asia and retrieves the map of its circuits. Revealed by Der Spiegel and Le Monde in December 2013.
b366ee419c: Rubio backs Orbán in Budapest before the vote
Visiting Budapest, Marco Rubio backs Viktor Orbán's re-election: “we want you to continue”. He links the “golden age” of bilateral relations to his staying in power. Orbán loses the 12 April vote.
b36ef9a798: Marines land at Fuzhou to protect the American consulate. Listed in Congressional Research Service report R42738.
b3772c61e3: An NSA memo revealed by Katharine Gun asks for spying on six undecided delegations before the Iraq vote.
b37962faf6: For the first time, the 8th Air Force takes the city center as its aiming point, on a Sunday as churchgoers leave Mass. Hundreds of civilians are killed.
b37b95612e: A U.S.-led unit kills eight to ten residents, including schoolchildren, in a night raid. The Afghan investigation speaks of executions. NATO acknowledges non-combatant casualties.
b388a21b59: According to Danish television DR, Americans linked to Trump are mapping supporters and opponents to promote secession. Copenhagen summons the chargé d'affaires.
b3a9bd6e6a: Before NATO, John Foster Dulles warns that rejection of the European Defense Community would force an “agonizing reappraisal” of American policy. The French Assembly rejects it in 1954.
b3c0190c85: Trump designates Nigeria a “country of particular concern” for religious freedom and threatens military intervention if the killings of Christians continue. Abuja rejects the accusation.
b488b4f11e: Bombing of the village of Karam
Strikes destroy the village of Karam. The Taliban report more than 100 dead. The Pentagon says it targeted caves and disputes the toll.
b4902047ec: In a cable revealed by WikiLeaks, Ambassador Craig Stapleton recommends drawing up a retaliation list against the EU and France for their rejection of GMOs.
b4a13c2ec8: End of Hong Kong's special status
Trump signs the Hong Kong Autonomy Act and an executive order that strips Hong Kong of its preferential treatment, after the national security law.
b4b8aa41d0: The group of General Camilo Valenzuela, backed by the CIA as part of Track II, fails to kidnap army chief René Schneider, an obstacle to a coup against Allende. Schneider is killed three days later in another attempt.
b4e36ca743: Trump backs De la Espriella in Colombia
Ahead of the June 21 runoff, Trump gives his “complete and total” support to far-right candidate Abelardo de la Espriella. The Petro government denounces electoral interference.
b4ffeb23bf: After the murder of Jamal Khashoggi, Trump says MBS “might have known, might not have” and maintains the alliance, against the view of the CIA, which attributes the order to the crown prince.
b50a37d81a: A U.S. Navy EP-3 on an eavesdropping mission collides with a Chinese fighter, whose pilot dies. The crew is held for eleven days.
b5112c9c7b: After the seizure of the freighter Mayaguez, the Marines attack Koh Tang island when the crew has already been released.
b516711a9d: Visas denied to the Palestinian delegation
The State Department revokes or denies the visas of Mahmoud Abbas and Palestinian officials ahead of the General Assembly, despite the UN headquarters agreement.
b52ce6c87d: U.S. aircraft strike fleeing fighters near the Kenyan border. Nomads are among the victims according to NGOs.
b5436fb1d2: Cuba must lease Guantánamo Bay to the United States, with no expiration date. The base is still there.
b582c2f440: Air America and the opium trade
Historian Alfred McCoy documents the transport of opium by CIA-linked aircraft for Lao allies. The CIA denies any direct involvement.
b5b059daea: Prosecuted over Technip's bribes in Brazil and FMC's in Iraq, the Franco-American group TechnipFMC reaches a 301 million dollar agreement with US justice, shared with Brazil.
b635c52bd7: Trial of Rolando Cubela in Havana

Cubela is arrested and tried for plotting with the CIA against Castro. The prosecutor demands the death penalty; Castro asks for clemency and Cubela is sentenced to 25 years in prison. The AMLASH plot is confirmed by the Church Committee.
b656cad508: Kissinger has a policy of rapprochement adopted toward the white regimes and Portugal, seen as durable. Arms delivered to Lisbon via NATO are used in its colonial wars.
b67e66e5fb: Western Enterprises, a CIA front, creates with the Taiwanese air force a unit for low-altitude night flights over China. It loses 15 aircraft and 148 men.
b68b4cf769: North Korea captures the NSA spy ship USS Pueblo off Wonsan. The crew is held for eleven months and Washington signs an apology to obtain their release.
b6976654e5: This internal catalog of the TAO unit offers some fifty tools: backdoors for Cisco, Juniper and Huawei, hard-drive firmware, fake cell towers, booby-trapped cables. Revealed by Der Spiegel in December 2013.
b69e02cc59: During the Tet Offensive, artillery and aircraft raze much of the town. An officer tells the AP that “it became necessary to destroy the town to save it”.
b6adecf1db: The American military government refuses to recognize the People's Republic of Korea and its local committees, then Hodge declares it illegal. He relies on the colonial-era administration and police.
b6b81851d5: Morales suspends the activities of the U.S. counternarcotics agency, accused of political espionage and of supporting the opposition. Washington rejects these accusations.
b6bbf6eb1a: Two weeks after the Washington-backed secession, the Frenchman Bunau-Varilla signs on behalf of Panama a treaty that cedes to the United States, in perpetuity, a canal zone where it acts as sovereign.
b6ce2b17c6: Battle of Rumaila after the ceasefire
Two days after the ceasefire, the 24th Infantry Division destroys a retreating Iraqi column. Journalist Seymour Hersh saw a massacre; the army concluded it was a legitimate response.
b6d670d252: The Wall Street Journal reveals that US military personnel are secretly training the Taiwanese army; President Tsai Ing-wen confirms it.
b6ed1bc99c: Greek shipowner of the Suez Rajan convicted
The Greek company Empire Navigation pleads guilty before American justice to transporting Iranian oil and pays 2.4 million dollars. About one million barrels seized are unloaded in Houston.
b73dfc3d8a: General Pershing enters Mexico with about 10,000 men to hunt down Pancho Villa, without capturing him, until 1917.
b74558a7ec: Strike on the Syrian army at Deir ez-Zor
Coalition aircraft bomb Syrian army positions and kill dozens of soldiers. Washington cites an error; the Russian-American truce collapses.
b75e5429ae: Physician Richard Strong, of the colonial Bureau of Science, induces beriberi in prisoners at Bilibid Prison through a deficient diet. These trials were cited at the Nuremberg Doctors' Trial.
b79048fe86: After a Sudanese city is bombed by a Libyan aircraft, Washington sends an AWACS surveillance aircraft to Egypt at the request of Sudan and Egypt. Listed in Congressional Research Service report R42738.
b7a267517b: The US 12th Air Force opens a series of Allied raids on Zara, then Italian, which last until October 1944. About 80% of the buildings are destroyed; death toll estimates range from under 1,000 to 4,000.
b7da51360c: A Saudi coalition strike kills 40 children on a bus. CNN identifies a laser-guided bomb made by Lockheed Martin and sold by the United States.
b81eaf5ac4: Embassy comments on the death of Quentin Deranque

The American embassy attributes on social media the death of the far-right activist to the far left. Paris sees it as instrumentalisation; Charles Kushner does not attend his summons and loses his direct access to ministers.
b83b19ea38: President Reagan says Ríos Montt is getting a “bum rap”, in the midst of the massacre campaign in the Mayan villages. Washington later resumes military sales.
b8711523c8: A blue mold epidemic ravages the Cuban tobacco crop. Havana accuses the United States of introducing it. No public proof establishes this.
b87c795b7f: Jiang Zemin's plane riddled with bugs
Beijing discovers 27 bugs in the presidential Boeing 767 fitted out in the United States. Chinese sources accuse U.S. intelligence; the CIA declines to comment.
b8a06b1dfe: The barracks where Gaddafi lives is among the targets. Investigations, including Seymour Hersh's, conclude that his death was sought; Washington has denied it.
b8a1a4fb06: A $100 million drawdown of artillery, ammunition and counter-battery radars.
b8a70029fa: Washington concludes that Moscow used a chemical agent against Sergei Skripal and announces sanctions under the chemical weapons law.
b8a7678042: Clinton signs the Iraq Liberation Act, which makes the overthrow of Saddam Hussein official policy and funds the Iraqi opposition to the tune of 97 million dollars.
b8b2216420: Marines land during the Liberal revolt of La Chambelona and remain until the early 1920s to protect the sugar plantations.
b8c9b7f7bd: To punish the neutrality of the Farrell and Perón military regime, Washington freezes Argentine gold assets in the United States and refuses to recognize the government.
b8d5700c4a: Operation Wappen: Damascus exposes a CIA plot with Syrian officers and expels three American diplomats.
b8dacfe2d1: Trump threatens with tariffs eight European countries that sent troops to Greenland, before backing down after a framework agreement reached with NATO in Davos.
b8e346ee44: According to Der Spiegel, the NSA monitors international financial transactions, notably through the SWIFT banking network, based in Belgium.
b8e50af017: Under threat of U.S. prosecution, UBS pays $780 million and hands over to the U.S. tax authorities data on its clients, a breach in Swiss bank secrecy.
b8f617668c: During his visit, Trump announces $110 billion in arms sales to Saudi Arabia, then engaged in the war in Yemen.
b8f92d2871: C-17 aircraft drop about fifty tons of ammunition to the Syrian Arab Coalition, allied with Kurdish militias, shortly after the abandonment of the “train and equip” program.
b8ff458b51: The NSA and GCHQ infiltrate World of Warcraft, Second Life and Xbox Live; the targets mentioned range from Chinese hackers to an Iranian nuclear scientist. No foiled plot is cited. Revealed by The Guardian, the NYT and ProPublica in December 2013.
b982efa1e8: A $500 million drawdown with 30 Bradleys, 25 Strykers and ammunition.
b98a63e036: Thai battalions in Laos for the CIA
The CIA recruits, pays and commands thousands of Thai “volunteers” to fight in Laos, from its headquarters at Udorn. A Senate report reveals them in 1971.
b98d72d7aa: Somalia declared an “area of active hostilities”
Donald Trump declares southern Somalia an “area of active hostilities,” which loosens the rules of engagement and exempts strikes from White House approval. The number of strikes rises sharply.
b9a64144a5: Chiquita's subsidiary pays 1.7 million dollars to the AUC until 2004. The firm pleads guilty in 2007; a Florida jury finds it liable for eight murders in 2024.
b9aa004be3: A Coast Guard team boards the tanker Veronica before dawn, the sixth vessel seized for defying the blockade of Venezuela-linked tankers.
b9ace6663d: Trump threatens to impose 100% tariffs on all Canadian goods if Ottawa concludes a trade deal with China, a week after approving it.
b9e9b352dc: During the announcement of the sanctions on PDVSA, John Bolton displays a notepad reading “5,000 troops to Colombia,” a signal of military pressure.
ba6d977be1: According to Der Spiegel, the NSA hacked the email account of Mexican President Felipe Calderón.
ba820b1884: Partial lifting of the military embargo
Reagan authorizes the sale of helicopter spare parts to the Guatemalan army, despite the massacres in the Mayan highlands.
ba8c2b9b56: Condoleezza Rice requests $75 million to fund Persian-language media, NGOs and Iranian opposition figures. Congress votes part of it.
ba8f0d3a44: Through IBAD, Washington funds candidates hostile to João Goulart. Ambassador Lincoln Gordon later mentioned about $5 million.
ba99f7140d: Rolls-Royce pays $170 million to the United States
